Looking at the cuboid (4×2×2), the visible white cubes are the bottom-front cube (position 2) and the top-back cube (position 2). The light grey piece occupies the left end (front-bottom, front-top, top-back-left, and top-front-left... i.e., a corner shape), the black piece occupies the right-back region, and the dark grey piece takes the remaining bottom-back cube next to it.

Filling in the hidden cubes: the white piece must connect its top-back cube to its bottom-front cube through the hidden bottom-back cube at position 2, and its fourth cube is the hidden bottom-back cube at position 1. So the white piece consists of a central cube with three arms extending in mutually perpendicular directions (left, front, and up) — a "corner" tetracube.

Checking the options:
- A, B, E are zigzag (twisted) shapes,
- D is a T-shape,
- C is exactly the corner shape: an L of three cubes with the fourth cube stacked on the corner cube.

Rotating the white piece appropriately matches diagram C.

\boxed{C}
